newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls Tajik hostage-taking act of terrorism.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls Tajik hostage-taking act of terrorism.

text.p: The United States on Thursday condemned the taking of hostages in Tajikistan as an "act of terrorism" and called on the Tajik government to do everything possible to resolve the crisis.
Four employees of the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR were kidnapped on Thursday by assailants believed to have seized up to 12 others in the remote Central Asian state.

"The U.S. government expresses its deep concern ... and condemns this act of terrorism," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a statement. He said that while the hostage-takers were "not formally under government subordination, the government of Tajikistan bears full responsibility for ensuring security in the country."
"We call upon the government to take all measures necessary to resolve this crisis immediately," he added.
Reports from Tajikistan say the hostage-takers are part of a group commanded by Rizyon Sadirov, who used to fight for the Islamic opposition but whose loyalties are now unclear.
Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov has vowed to work for the hostages' release.
